key_insight: Modeling a molecule as a conformational ensemble, rather than a single structure, improves cyclic-peptide property prediction.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests ensemble-aware graph models can be used to build more accurate predictive tools for molecular design and screening in computational chemistry and drug discovery.
method: Encode each conformer with shared EGNN layers.
Pool conformer embeddings using a Set Attention Block to form one ensemble representation.
Pretrain with masked token recovery, noisy-coordinate reconstruction, and pairwise distance reconstruction.
evidence_signal: On CREMP-CycPeptMPDB, training from scratch failed (R^2=0.005), while pretrained EnsembleEGNN achieved R^2=0.477 and Pearson r=0.699, and the BERT+EnsembleEGNN hybrid improved further to R^2=0.538 and r=0.737.
watch_item: Performance depends on access to high-quality conformer ensembles, so generating and curating reliable ensemble data may be a practical bottleneck.
paper_title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
